summary: Alessia Russo scored twice as Arsenal clinched a much-needed 2-1 win over Liverpool at Anfield.3 min: Endemann looks to send a cross towards the back post from the right but the ball runs behind.2 min: Arsenal drive forward early and look to pile on the pressure.

stories.title: Russo on target again as double fires under-pressure Arsenal to vital WSL win at Liverpool
summary: Alessia Russo scored twice at Anfield to provide the under-pressure Arsenal head coach, Renée Slegers, with some brief respite but it was another unconvincing display from the north Londoners despite their much-needed 2-1 victory.The in-form Russo’s double took her recent tally to seven goals in her past four appearances and 10 in her past seven games for club and country, but Liverpool posed plenty of problems for the visitors and were unhappy about a disallowed goal.

summary: Kangaroos beat Toa Samoa 44-12 at Sydney’s Allianz StadiumNew Zealand await Australia in next weekend’s men’s final This was supposed to be Samoa’s chance to challenge the wilting Kangaroos, whose patchy recent performance made them appear vulnerable – to make up for the loss in the last World Cup final, when Australia kept Toa Samoa scoreless for much of that defeat at Old Trafford.So when the famed Siva Tau, Samoa’s pre-match ritual, brought the Samoans and the Australians close enough to kiss, the anticipation for this semi-final could not have been higher; the match seemed almost certain to explode.

stories.title: Australia 30-14 Fiji: Women’s Rugby League World Cup semi-final – as it happened
summary: Fiji Bulikula level at half-time but Jillaroos surge away after breakHosts to meet New Zealand in next weekend’s final5th minute (Australia 0-0 Fiji): The Jillaroos have weathered some serious attack from Fiji but they’ve got the ball back and now try to settle.

She rises slowly and the Jillaroos thump it downfield through the boot of Tarryn Aiken.3rd minute (Australia 0-0 Fiji): Australia’s Abbie Church has been run over the sideline and now it’s Fiji on the attack.
They launch wave after wave but can’t snap the golden line.

stories.title: Abbi Church powers Australia to win over spirited Fiji as hosts reach Women’s Rugby League World Cup final
summary: Church scores four tries as Australia beat Fiji Bulikula 30-14 Jillaroos will face New Zealand in the final next weekendThe Jillaroos survived an almighty scare from Fiji in the World Cup semi-final, securing a place in the tournament decider against New Zealand at Lang Park next week despite a stunning resistance from the brilliant Bulikula.Driven by the exquisite, unpredictable playmaker Luisa Yaranamua – 23 and yet to play an NRLW match – and supported by powerful, committed teammates, Fiji led for much of the first half and were level with the Jillaroos at half-time.

stories.title: Another No 1 falls as Notre Dame hold off Miami to shake up college football playoff race
summary: Carr throws for 319 yards and three TDs in 31-24 winNo 4 Irish avenge loss that cost them playoff berthMiami comeback falls short after disputed late callCJ Carr threw for 319 yards and three touchdowns as No 4 Notre Dame avenged their most damaging loss of last season, racing to a 21-point lead before holding on to beat top-ranked Miami 31-24 on Saturday night.Micah Gilbert caught two of Carr’s touchdown passes, Jordan Faison had the other and Nolan James Jr added a rushing score for Notre Dame (8-1, No 11 College Football Playoff), who entered the game knowing another defeat to Miami could derail their national championship hopes.

stories.title: Messi claims second straight Golden Boot as Nashville set points record on MLS Decision Day
summary: Messi first to win consecutive MLS Golden BootsInter Miami surrender 3-0 lead in dramatic draw Nashville set new league record with 77 pointsLionel Messi won his second consecutive MLS Golden Boot award on Saturday, but Inter Miami squandered a three-goal lead in a 3-3 draw with Charlotte on the final day of the regular season.The Argentinian superstar failed to score but set up Miami’s first two goals from corners at Nu Stadium as the defending champions secured second place in the Eastern Conference and home-field advantage for the first two rounds of the playoffs.
